UPSTREAM: drivers/intel/fsp2_0: fix TPM setup and MRC cache hash logic When VBOOT_STARTS_IN_BOOTBLOCK is selected, the tpm_setup call in memory_init.c is not used. When VBOOT_STARTS_IN_ROMSTAGE is selected, the tpm_setup call in memory_init.c is triggered. However, when verstage runs, tpm_setup is called yet again, and an error is triggered from the multiple initialization calls. Since there are currently no boards using VBOOT_STARTS_IN_ROMSTAGE + FSP2_0_USES_TPM_MRC_HASH, disable this combination via Kconfig, and remove the tpm_setup call from Intel FSP memory initializion code. * VBOOT=y VBOOT_STARTS_IN_BOOTBLOCK=y vboot is enabled, and TPM is setup prior to Intel FSP memory initialization. Allow FSP2_0_USES_TPM_MRC_HASH option. * VBOOT=y VBOOT_STARTS_IN_BOOTBLOCK=n vboot is enabled, but TPM is setup in romstage, after Intel FSP memory initialization. Disallow FSP2_0_USES_TPM_MRC_HASH option. * VBOOT=n vboot is disabled. Disallow FSP2_0_USES_TPM_MRC_HASH option. See bug for more information: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=940377 BUG=chromium:940377 TEST=util/lint/checkpatch.pl -g origin/master..HEAD TEST=util/abuild/abuild -B -e -y -c 50 -p none -x TEST=make clean && make test-abuild BRANCH=none Change-Id: I490d0fc52fce3e8906c7f461cf63406d32560265 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 2c8243cf6de4726092b8ff31a73d633ec58baaab Original-Change-Id: I4ba91c275c33245be61041cb592e52f861dbafe6 Original-Signed-off-by: Joel Kitching <kitching@google.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/c/coreboot/+/31837 Original-Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1524798 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: Add required FSP UPD changes for CML This patch adds required FSP UPD changes for CometLake SoC. Also this patch tries to create common parse logic for CometLake as well as cannonlake SOC. We parse device tree parameters for PCI devices and fill values in FSP UPDs. We fill UPDs based on pci device config as well as SerialIoDev config of devicetree. For PCI devices, if PCI device is disabled from devicetree, we'll assign disable value to FSP UPD. In case devicetree doesn't fill this parameter or value is invalid in SerialIoDev config, default mode will be set to PCI. In case of valid value, we'll fill the same value into FSP UPD. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=check if CML board boots and proper UPD values are filled. UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: Pass coreboot debug interface info to FSP coreboot have an option to use legacy UART or LPSS UART. FSP will use the UART initialized by coreboot and we can choose an option to skip Uart initialization by FSP. For this, we need to pass correct debug interface flag to FSP through which FSP will know which UART port to use. If we don't pass correct interface information, FSP may try to dump logs on that port and it may slow down the system. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=Compile and boot with coreboot. Check FSP and coreboot logs are coming on serial port. diagnostics: add status_message field to GetRoutineUpdateResponse. GetRoutineUpdateResponse has a single field, output, which holds both the result of a routine, e.g. "Failed to start the urandom executable" as well as any accumulated logs. Add a new field to GetRoutineUpdateResponse, status_message, to hold the result of a routine, and let output be only the accumulated logs. This allows for a routine like battery_sysfs to separate the log messages from a detailed status message. BUG=chromium:919151 TEST=manual and unit tests Change-Id: I6935d73dcc99ced9fe6ef7a1e6fe72b22b518d94 Signed-off-by: Paul Moy <pmoy@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1516235

dependency: fix bug that causes dependency source paths to be incorrect Currently, many sources paths in the resulted json deps file are prefixed with the directory which the build_api script is invoked with. e.g: "/mnt/host/source/src/third_party/chromiumos-overlay/eclass" This is because of a bug in how source paths are handled in dependency. After the source paths, they are converted to relative paths with respect to CHROOT_SOURCE_ROOT. Then to filter out paths that are subdirectories of others, they are converted to absolute path again using os.path.abspath(..), but this instead uses the current directory script is invoked with as the root directory. This CLs fixes the problem by not converting source paths to relative path before filtering out subdirectories. It also add check in NormalizeSourcePaths() method to ensure that all the input paths are absolute paths. TEST=run `./bin/build_api chromite.api.DependencyService/GetBuildDependencyGraph --input-json=input.json --output-json=output.json` and verify all the source paths look correct BUG=chromium:938605 Change-Id: Ibd0ed9587c9e6dbce7773a4b47c869beecb67eff Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1525869 Commit-Ready: Ned Nguyen <nednguyen@google.com> Tested-by: Ned Nguyen <nednguyen@google.com> Reviewed-by: Ned Nguyen <nednguyen@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Abraham <seanabraham@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Klein <saklein@chromium.org>
